title.narrative: Water Resources Development Investment Program - Project 2

description.narrative: The proposed Lower Kokcha Irrigation Project (LKIP) will rehabilitate and improve the Shahrawan and Archi canals. Both canals suffer under both scour and sedimentation and water levels (Shahrawan canal) and capacity (Archi canal) are compromised if no works are undertaken. The Shahrawan intake, the approach channel and outflow channel have degraded significantly and are in danger of being washed away. Failure of water delivery would negatively impact around 46,000 ha of crops. The Shahrawan intake headworks will be rehabilitated and upgraded to fully discharge its design flow (60 m3/s) in a controlled manner into the Shahrawan canal. The Archi main canal will be rehabilitated and upgraded to its original design capacity of 36 m3/s (current flow rate is estimated at 30 m3/s). The flow capacity of the canal will continually degrade in the future in the absence of the project, further reducing the current area of crops of 23,041 ha (ie 85.3% crop intensity). The technology proposed is compatible with local conditions and comprises mostly unlined canals, with lined canals in areas of high flows. The project will strengthen water management institutions through creating irrigation and water users associations, and strengthening river basin and sub-basin authorities. To ensure sufficient operations and maintenance (O&M) the concept of an irrigation service fee will be introduced in Lower Kokcha Irrigation Scheme (LKIS), tied to equity and reliability of water supply and incremental benefits.

description.narrative: Improved water resources management in the Lower Kokcha Irrigation System

Cropping intensity in 2019 in LKIS is 155% (2013 = 122%) Progress/Status: All the eight main civil works contracts for rehabilitation of Shahrawan and Archi main canals in Lower Kokcha irrigation system have been awarded. Out of these contracts, one contract for rehabilitation of intake was completed in January 2021 and another contract for intake rehabilitation was completed and handed over in April 2021. Activities of the rest of civil works contracts were extensively delayed due to safeguards issues. As per grant agreement the Previous Government (the Government) was responsible for compensating any losses occurred due to project implementation. However, the Government could not pay affected households (AH) due to shortage of state fund which further delayed project implementation. On 26 Feb 2020 the Government requested ADB to allow utilization of grant proceeds for compensation which was approved by ADB through a minor change memo on 3 May 2020. Payment to AH was once again delayed as the implementing agency, the Ministry of Energy and Water (MEW) was dissolved into two new entities of National Water Affairs Regulatory Authority (NAWARA) and Energy Services Regulatory Authority (ESRA). The new entity (NWARA) was not as much authorized as MEW was, which hampered delivery of compensation to the AH. In December 2020 NWARA managed to secure special authority for delivering the compensation and paid most of the AH except for a few who were absent during the payment process. With the previous government deposed in mid-August 2021, all the project related activities have been disrupted and this target is likely to be further delayed since contractors and NGOs have stopped working. Moreover, ADB has placed hold on its assistance in Afghanistan following fall of the previous government, effective 15 August 2021. Data Source: MEW's quarterly reporting Actual value:
